blame_rule: git blame -w -M -C --first-parent at the pinned commit; committer
time per line (a branch merged later is dated by its merge; moved
or copied lines keep their original date)
a question is 'after' when at least half of its key's non-blank
lines changed after the cutoff day (23:59:59 UTC)
key lines: locate = the function; callers = the call lines of
key callers and open disputes; flow = every candidate hop's

scope.code: every tracked .py outside tests/, test/, examples/, docs/

scoring.locate: file + function; a function nested inside the key function also counts
scoring.callers: the set of direct callers (file + function, or file + <module> for top-level code), outside tests/, examples/, docs/
scoring.flow: the required hops Han marks, recalled, in order (LCS); hops in neither the trace nor the AST count as invented

flow_rules: keep: the subtree under the question's entry call(s), repo
calls only (the T3 filter: package source, no tests)
drop with callees: logging and metrics:
drop with callees: folded calls (fold = one hop, callees
drop, keep callees: generator re-entries (resume events);
a generator counts once, where it was created
drop, keep callees: trivial functions (one statement: a
return with no call, or a get_/is_/has_ return)
merge: a function called again counts once, at its first

ast_resolution.name: plain name: same-module function, nested function or import
ast_resolution.class: class called by name -> its __init__ (found up the repo bases)
ast_resolution.self: self.m() / cls.m() -> m on the class or its repo bases
ast_resolution.override: self.m() -> an override of m in a repo subclass (class hierarchy analysis)
ast_resolution.super: super().m() -> m on a repo base class
ast_resolution.module: module.f() on an imported repo module
ast_resolution.classattr: Class.m() on a repo class named in the code

dispute_kinds.attr: obj.m() on an object whose type the AST cannot see; m matches the target by name only
dispute_kinds.getattr: getattr(obj, 'm') with the target's name as a string
dispute_kinds.reference: the target passed or stored without being called (callback, registry, decorator)

questions.text: Where is a query sent to the Exa API, with each result's title, URL and highlights turned into a result entry?
Where are arbitrary values, bytes included, turned into a string that is safe to print to the console, with ASCII control characters replaced by visible escape codes?
Where is the limit on how long model-written code may run enforced, by running it in a one-worker thread pool and raising an error if it hasn't finished in time?
When code runs in a remote sandbox, where is the encoded answer it sends back decoded, choosing JSON or pickle by a prefix and rejecting pickle unless it was allowed?
Where are Python values such as tuples, sets, bytes, dates, numpy arrays and images converted into plain JSON structures tagged with type markers?
Where is a value encoded into a prefixed string for the remote executor, JSON-only by default, falling back to pickle with a warning only when that is allowed?
Where is model-written code rewritten so that assigning to a variable with the same name as the answer-returning tool does not shadow that tool?
After a model has returned its full reply, where is that text trimmed at the stop strings (shared helper, and a reply with no content is passed through unchanged)?
Where is long output shortened to a maximum length by keeping its first and last halves with a notice in between?
Before a tool runs, where are string arguments that match the name of a stored value swapped for that value?
Where are streamed chunks of a model reply merged into one message, concatenating partial tool-call arguments by index and adding up token counts?
Where does a model client sleep so that its requests stay under a requests-per-minute limit?
